sections.heading: POINT PLACEMENT
sections.content:
Point placement in `CutTool` (`UnityEditor.ProBuilder.CutTool`) coordinates mouse interactions, raycasting, geometric snapping to vertices and edges, path validation, and point modification.

1. Raycasting and Surface Hit Detection:
- During `OnToolGUI(EditorWindow window)`, the method `DoPointPlacement(window)` executes every frame.
- Surface picking is evaluated by `UpdateHitPosition()`: it transforms the GUI mouse coordinate into a 3D ray using `UHandleUtility.GUIPointToWorldRay(evt.mousePosition)` and tests against the target mesh via `UnityEngine.ProBuilder.HandleUtility.FaceRaycast(ray, m_Mesh, out pbHit)`.
- If a face is hit, `UpdateCurrentPosition(Face face, Vector3 position, Vector3 normal)` sets `m_CurrentFace = face`, `m_CurrentPosition = position`, `m_CurrentPositionNormal = normal`, and initializes `m_CurrentVertexTypes = VertexTypes.None`.

2. Snapping to Existing Cut Points (`CheckPointInCutPath`):
- Snapping to the start point (loop closure): If `!m_ModifyingPoint && m_CutPath.Count > 1`, proximity to `m_CutPath[0].position` is tested with a fixed threshold of `0.1f` using `Math.Approx3(vertexData.position, m_CurrentPosition, 0.1f)`. When matched, `m_CurrentPosition` snaps to `vertexData.position`, `m_CurrentVertexTypes` is assigned `vertexData.types | VertexTypes.VertexInShape`, and `m_SelectedIndex = 0`.
- Snapping to arbitrary cut points: When `m_SnappingPoint` (active if `m_SnapToGeometry` is enabled or Ctrl is held: `(evt.modifiers & EventModifiers.Control) != 0`) or `m_ModifyingPoint` (active if Shift is held: `evt.shift`) is true, the tool searches all vertices in `m_CutPath` within `m_SnappingDistance` (default `0.1f`, key `VertexInsertion.snappingDistance`). The closest vertex index is stored in `m_SelectedIndex`, its types are bitwise-ORed with `VertexTypes.VertexInShape`, and `m_CurrentPosition` snaps to the vertex position (if not modifying).

3. Snapping to Mesh Vertices and Edges (`CheckPointInMesh`):
- Invoked when `m_CurrentVertexTypes == VertexTypes.None && !m_ModifyingPoint`. Defaults `m_CurrentVertexTypes = VertexTypes.NewVertex`.
- Boundary edges of the current/target face are retrieved in loop order using `WingedEdge.SortEdgesByAdjacency`.
- Vertex snapping: Compares `m_CurrentPosition` against edge start vertices `vertices[peripheralEdges[i].a].position` using `Math.Approx3` with distance threshold `m_SnappingDistance` (or `0.01f` when `m_TargetFace == null && !m_SnappingPoint`). When cursor hovers outside the target face (`m_CurrentFace != m_TargetFace`), vertex proximity `vertexDist` takes strict precedence over edge proximity `edgeDist` whenever `vertexDist <= bestDistance`.
- When a vertex snap is detected: `m_CurrentPosition = vertices[peripheralEdges[bestIndex].a].position`, `m_CurrentVertexTypes = VertexTypes.ExistingVertex`, `m_SelectedIndex = -1`, `m_SnapedVertexId = peripheralEdges[bestIndex].a`, followed by a call to `CheckPointInCutPath()`.
- Edge snapping: When no vertex snap matches but an edge is within `bestDistance`, the point is orthogonally projected:
  - If `m_TargetFace == null || m_TargetFace == m_CurrentFace`, projection along segment `[left, right]` is computed as:
    `float x = (m_CurrentPosition - left).magnitude;`
    `float y = (m_CurrentPosition - right).magnitude;`
    `m_CurrentPosition = left + (x / (x + y)) * (right - left);`
  - If `m_CurrentFace != m_TargetFace`, the hit is projected onto the infinite line of the target face peripheral edge:
    `Vector3 a = m_CurrentPosition - vertices[peripheralEdges[bestIndex].a].position;`
    `Vector3 b = vertices[peripheralEdges[bestIndex].b].position - vertices[peripheralEdges[bestIndex].a].position;`
    `float angle = Vector3.Angle(b, a);`
    `m_CurrentPosition = Vector3.Magnitude(a) * Mathf.Cos(angle * Mathf.Deg2Rad) * b / Vector3.Magnitude(b) + vertices[peripheralEdges[bestIndex].a].position;`
  - Sets `m_SnapedEdge = peripheralEdges[bestIndex]`, `m_CurrentVertexTypes = VertexTypes.AddedOnEdge`, and `m_SelectedIndex = -1`.

4. Point Addition and Path Construction:
- `CanAppendCurrentPointToPath()` verifies: (a) `Math.IsNumber(m_CurrentPosition)` is true; (b) `polyCount == 0 || m_SelectedIndex != polyCount - 1` (cannot click same vertex twice consecutively); (c) no intermediate point duplicates: `for (int i = 1; i < polyCount; i++) if (Math.Approx3(m_CutPath[i].position, m_CurrentPosition)) return false;`; (d) loop completion is permitted only when `polyCount >= 3`.
- `AddCurrentPositionToPath(bool optimize = true)`: Registers undo `UndoUtility.RecordObject(this, "Add Vertex On Path")`. If `m_TargetFace == null`, binds `m_TargetFace = m_CurrentFace` and caches `m_SelectedVertices` and `m_SelectedEdges`. Appends `new CutVertexData(m_CurrentPosition, m_CurrentPositionNormal, m_CurrentVertexTypes)` to `m_CutPath`, sets `m_PlacingPoint = true`, `m_SelectedIndex = m_CutPath.Count - 1`, and calls `RebuildCutShape(optimize)`.

5. Point Modification / Dragging:
- When Shift is held (`m_ModifyingPoint`), left-clicking an existing point sets `m_PlacingPoint = true`.
- On `EventType.MouseDrag`, if `hasHitPosition && m_SelectedIndex >= 0`, updates `m_CutPath[m_SelectedIndex].position = m_CurrentPosition` and flags `m_Dirty = true`.
- On `MouseUp`, `Ignore`, `KeyDown`, or `KeyUp`, resets `m_PlacingPoint = false` and `m_SelectedIndex = -1`.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, raycasting to mesh faces in tool viewports is implemented using `Camera3D.project_ray_origin` and `Camera3D.project_ray_normal` with triangle intersection math or `PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D`. Snapping to edges/vertices can be computed against `ArrayMesh` surfaces using `Geometry3D.get_closest_point_to_segment`.

sections.heading: VISUAL FEEDBACK
sections.content:
The visual feedback system in `CutTool` renders path segments, preview guide lines, mesh connections, vertex handles, face overlays, and contextual cursors.

1. Color Palette and Constants:
- `k_HandleColor`: `new Color(0.8f, 0.8f, 0.8f, 1f)` (light gray default handle color).
- `k_HandleColorAddNewVertex`: `new Color(0.01f, 0.9f, 0.3f, 1f)` (bright green for new vertices on face).
- `s_HandleColorAddVertexOnEdge`: `Handles.selectedColor` (cyan/blue for splitting an existing edge; fallback `new Color(0.3f, 0.01f, 0.9f, 1f)`).
- `s_HandleColorUseExistingVertex`: `Handles.selectedColor` (cyan/blue for snapping to an existing vertex; fallback `new Color(0.01f, 0.5f, 1f, 1f)`).
- `k_HandleColorModifyVertex`: `new Color(1f, 0.75f, 0.0f, 1f)` (amber/orange when Shift-modifying an existing point).
- `k_LineColor`: `new Color(0f, 55f / 255f, 1f, 1f)` (deep blue for valid cut paths).
- `k_InvalidLineColor`: `Color.red` (red for self-intersecting or overlapping cuts).
- `k_ConnectionsLineColor`: `new Color(0f, 200f / 255f, 170f / 200f, 1f)` (teal for connection lines to boundary vertices).
- `k_DrawingLineColor`: `new Color(0.01f, 0.9f, 0.3f, 1f)` (bright green for the active cursor guide line).
- `k_HandleSize`: `0.05f` multiplier applied to `HandleUtility.GetHandleSize(point)`.

2. Vertex Dot Rendering:
- `DoExistingPointsGUI()`: Iterates through `m_CutPath`, transforms each position via `trs.TransformPoint(m_CutPath[index].position)`, computes size with `HandleUtility.GetHandleSize(point) * k_HandleSize`, and draws a dot handle using `Handles.DotHandleCap(-1, point, Quaternion.identity, size, evt.type)` colored with `k_HandleColor`.
- `DoCurrentPointsGUI()`: Transforms `m_CurrentPosition` (or `m_CutPath[m_SelectedIndex].position` when dragging) to world space and renders a dot cap with `m_CurrentHandleColor`.

3. Polyline and Guide Line Rendering:
- `DrawCutLine()`: Sets `Handles.color` to `m_IsCutValid ? k_LineColor : k_InvalidLineColor`, transforms all points in `m_CutPath` into world coordinates, and calls `Handles.DrawPolyLine`.
- `DrawGuideLine()`: If `m_CutPath.Count > 0` and `!m_ModifyingPoint`, draws a dotted line between `m_CutPath[m_CutPath.Count - 1].position` and `m_CurrentPosition` using `Handles.DrawDottedLine(..., 5f)` with `k_DrawingLineColor`.
- `DrawMeshConnectionsHandles()`: If `m_MeshConnections.Count > 0`, draws dotted lines between each cut vertex `m_CutPath[connection.item1].position` and target boundary vertex `vertices[connection.item2].position` using `Handles.DrawDottedLine(..., 5f)` in `k_ConnectionsLineColor`.

4. Geometry Highlighting (`DoVisualCues`):
- When `m_TargetFace == null && m_CurrentFace != null`, the hovered face is shaded using `EditorHandleDrawing.HighlightFaces(m_Mesh, new Face[]{m_CurrentFace}, Color.Lerp(Color.blue, Color.cyan, 0.5f))`.
- Mesh vertices and edges available for snapping are highlighted via `EditorHandleDrawing.HighlightVertices(m_Mesh, m_SelectedVertices, false)` and `EditorHandleDrawing.HighlightEdges(m_Mesh, m_SelectedEdges, false)`.
- When actively snapped, specific elements are highlighted: `m_SnapedVertexId != -1` highlights the vertex, and `m_SnapedEdge != Edge.Empty` highlights the edge.

5. Mouse Cursor Management:
- `cursorTexture` returns `m_CutCursorTexture` ("Cursors/cutCursor") when `m_CutPath.Count == 0`, and `m_CutAddCursorTexture` ("Cursors/cutCursor-add") when `m_CutPath.Count > 0`.
- Applied in `OnToolGUI` via `Cursor.SetCursor(m_CurrentCutCursor, Vector2.zero, CursorMode.Auto)` and registered with `SceneView.AddCursorRect(sceneViewRect, MouseCursor.CustomCursor)`.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, 3D viewport handles and lines can be rendered using `ImmediateMesh` with unshaded vertex colors or using `RenderingServer` 3D line drawing functions (`line_3d`). Dotted lines can be achieved using a custom shader with a stepped `fract(uv.x * dot_count)` alpha discard.

sections.heading: CUT EXECUTION
sections.content:
Cut execution in `CutTool` transforms the user-defined cut path into concrete topology modifications, splitting `m_TargetFace` into new polygon faces.

1. Completion Triggers:
- Keyboard: Pressing Return, KeypadEnter, or Space (`HandleKeyEvent`) invokes `ExecuteCut()` followed by `ExitTool()`.
- UI Button: Clicking "Complete" in the Cut Settings overlay GUI (`OnOverlayGUI`) calls `ExecuteCut()`.
- Automatic Loop Closure: When the user places a final point onto the starting vertex with `m_CutPath.Count >= 3`, `isALoop` evaluates to `true`. In `RebuildCutShape(optimize: true)`, if `m_IsCutValid` is `true`, `ExecuteCut()` is called automatically.
- Tool Deactivation: `OnWillBeDeactivated()` calls `ExecuteCut(restorePrevious: false)` to commit pending valid cuts.

2. Execution Pipeline in `DoCut()`:
- Validation: Checks `if (m_TargetFace == null || m_CutPath.Count < 2)` (returns `ActionResult.Status.Canceled`) and `if (!m_IsCutValid)` (returns `ActionResult.Status.Failure`).
- Undo Registration: `UndoUtility.RecordObject(m_Mesh, "Execute Cut")`.
- Vertex Snapshot & Insertion:
  - Snapshots initial connection vertices: `formerVertices[i] = meshVertices[m_MeshConnections[i].item2]`.
  - Dispatches vertex insertion via `InsertVertices()`:
    - `VertexTypes.ExistingVertex` / `VertexInShape`: Calls `InsertVertexOnExistingVertex(vertexData.position)` which searches `m_Mesh.GetVertices()` for an approx matching position with valid normal.
    - `VertexTypes.AddedOnEdge`: Calls `InsertVertexOnExistingEdge(vertexData.position)` which identifies the nearest peripheral edge of `m_TargetFace` using `Math.DistancePointLineSegment` and calls `m_Mesh.InsertVertexOnEdge(peripheralEdges[bestIndex], vertexPosition)`.
    - `VertexTypes.NewVertex`: Calls `m_Mesh.InsertVertexInMesh(vertexData.position, vertexData.normal)`.
  - Maps inserted vertex references to mesh indices `cutIndexes = cutVertices.Select(vert => meshVertices.IndexOf(vert)).ToArray()`.
  - Remaps `m_MeshConnections`: `connection.item1` becomes the new mesh index of `cutVertices[connection.item1]`, and `connection.item2` becomes the new mesh index of `formerVertices[i]`.

3. Closed Loop Creation:
- If `isALoop` is true:
  - Creates central face: `Face f = m_Mesh.CreatePolygon(cutIndexes, false)`.
  - Assigns `f.submeshIndex = m_TargetFace.submeshIndex`.
  - Computes normals `Vector3 nrm = Math.Normal(m_Mesh, f)` and `Vector3 targetNrm = Math.Normal(m_Mesh, m_TargetFace)`.
  - If `Vector3.Dot(nrm, targetNrm) < 0f`, inverts winding order via `f.Reverse()`.
  - Appends `f` to `newFaces`.

4. Outer/Subdivided Face Computation (`ComputeNewFaces`):
- Obtains continuous peripheral edges of `m_TargetFace` using `WingedEdge.SortEdgesByAdjacency(face)`.
- Maps edge vertex indices to shared universal indices via `m_Mesh.sharedVertexLookup`.
- Identifies `startIndex`: the first edge whose `.a` vertex matches a cut vertex shared index or a mesh connection endpoint.
- Traverses the peripheral edge loop from `startIndex` to `peripheralEdgesUnique.Count + startIndex`:
  - Appends `peripheralEdges[i % peripheralEdgesUnique.Count].a` to `polygon`.
  - When a cut vertex or connection endpoint is reached:
    - If a connection endpoint, appends `connection.item1` to `polygon`.
    - If `polygon.Count != 2`, invokes `ComputeFaceClosure(polygon, index, cutVertexSharedIndexes, out toDelete)`.
    - Assigns `newFace.submeshIndex = m_TargetFace.submeshIndex`, records `newFace` in `newFaces`, and aggregates `facesToDelete`.
    - Starts a new polygon list starting with the current peripheral edge vertex.
- Deletes temporary candidate faces: `m_Mesh.DeleteFaces(facesToDelete)`.
- If `!isALoop`, adds computed peripheral faces to `newFaces`.

5. Face Closure Path Resolution (`ComputeFaceClosure`):
- For a given starting peripheral polygon segment `polygonStart`, the algorithm searches both reverse and forward paths along `cutIndexes` starting at `startIndex = cutIndexes.IndexOf(currentIndex)`:
  - Reverse path: steps from `startIndex - 1` down to `finalIndex` (`startIndex - cutIndexes.Count` if loop, else 0), stopping when reaching `polygonFirstVertex` or `connection.item1`.
  - Forward path: steps from `startIndex + 1` up to `finalIndex` (`startIndex + cutIndexes.Count` if loop, else `cutIndexes.Count`), stopping when reaching `polygonFirstVertex` or `connection.item1`.
- For each connected candidate path:
  - Combines candidate path with `polygonStart` and creates a candidate face via `m_Mesh.CreatePolygon(closure, false)`.
  - Calculates polygon area via `Math.PolygonArea(vertices, indexes)`.
  - Selects the candidate face with minimal positive surface area (`area < bestArea`), marking all larger/enclosing candidate faces in `facesToDelete`.

6. Mesh Finalization:
- Collects helper vertex indices created solely for cut routing: `(data.types & VertexTypes.NewVertex) != 0 && (data.types & VertexTypes.VertexInShape) == 0`.
- Deletes temporary helper vertices: `m_Mesh.DeleteVertices(verticesIndexesToDelete)`.
- Deletes original face: `m_Mesh.DeleteFace(m_TargetFace)`.
- Reconstructs and cleans mesh buffers: `m_Mesh.ToMesh(); m_Mesh.Refresh(); m_Mesh.Optimize();`.
- Updates selection: `MeshSelection.ClearElementSelection(); m_Mesh.SetSelectedFaces(newFaces); ProBuilderEditor.Refresh();`.
- Calls `Clear()` to reset tool state.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, splitting an arbitrary polygon face requires sorting boundary half-edges and calculating polygon area via triangulation (or `Geometry2D.triangulate_polygon` projected onto the face plane). Area comparison guarantees that the smaller valid sub-polygon is preserved without self-overlap.

sections.heading: UNDO/CANCEL
sections.content:
The `CutTool` integrates with the Unity Undo system and provides keybindings and UI actions to delete points, cancel in-progress cuts, and recover state.

1. Backspace Point Deletion:
- Handled inside `HandleKeyEvent(Event evt)` on `KeyCode.Backspace`.
- If `m_CutPath.Count > 0`:
  - Records undo state on the mesh: `UndoUtility.RecordObject(m_Mesh, "Delete Selected Points")`.
  - Removes the last point in the list: `m_CutPath.RemoveAt(m_CutPath.Count - 1)`.
  - Sets `m_Dirty = true` to trigger `RebuildCutShape()` on the next update.
  - Consumes the event with `evt.Use()`.

2. Escape Key and Cancellation:
- Handled on `KeyCode.Escape` in `HandleKeyEvent` or clicking the "Cancel" button in `OnOverlayGUI`.
- Calls `ExitTool()`, which resets state via `Clear()` and restores the previous active tool via `ToolManager.RestorePreviousTool()`.
- `Clear()` resets `m_Mesh = null`, `m_TargetFace = null`, `m_CurrentFace = null`, `m_PlacingPoint = false`, `m_CurrentCutCursor = null`, `m_CutPath.Clear()`, `m_MeshConnections.Clear()`, `m_SelectedVertices = null`, `m_SelectedEdges = null`, calls `EditorHandleDrawing.ClearHandles()`, and refreshes the ProBuilder window via `ProBuilderEditor.Refresh()`.

3. Undo and Redo Callback Integration:
- The tool subscribes to `Undo.undoRedoPerformed += UndoRedoPerformed` in `OnActivated()` and unsubscribes in `OnWillBeDeactivated()`.
- Point additions record the tool instance: `UndoUtility.RecordObject(this, "Add Vertex On Path")` in `AddCurrentPositionToPath`.
- Full cut operations record the mesh instance: `UndoUtility.RecordObject(m_Mesh, "Execute Cut")` in `DoCut`.
- Inside `UndoRedoPerformed()`:
  - If `m_CutPath.Count == 0 && m_Mesh != null`, resets `m_TargetFace = null` and re-extracts `m_SelectedVertices` and `m_SelectedEdges` across all mesh faces.
  - Resets `m_SelectedIndex = -1`.
  - Clears `m_MeshConnections.Clear()`.
  - Sets `m_Dirty = true`, forcing recomputation of mesh boundary connections and cut shape validation in `RebuildCutShape()`.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4 editor plugins, undo/redo is implemented via `EditorUndoRedoManager`. Action registration wraps point additions and cut executions with `create_action`, `add_do_method`, and `add_undo_method`.

sections.heading: MULTI-FACE CUTS
sections.content:
Analysis of multi-face cut capabilities in `CutTool`:

1. Target Face Restriction:
- The ProBuilder `CutTool` is strictly constrained to a single target face (`m_TargetFace`).
- When the tool starts, `m_TargetFace` is `null`. Placing the first cut point binds `m_TargetFace = m_CurrentFace` inside `AddCurrentPositionToPath`:
  `m_TargetFace = m_CurrentFace;`
  `var edges = m_TargetFace.edges;`
  `m_SelectedVertices = edges.Select(e => e.a).ToArray();`
  `m_SelectedEdges = edges.ToArray();`

2. Behavior Across Multiple Faces:
- When the user moves the mouse cursor outside `m_TargetFace` onto another face (`m_CurrentFace != m_TargetFace`), the tool does not permit extending the cut path onto the adjacent face.
- In `CheckPointInMesh()`, the edge set is forced to the target face's boundary: `if (m_TargetFace != null && m_CurrentFace != m_TargetFace) peripheralEdges = WingedEdge.SortEdgesByAdjacency(m_TargetFace);`.
- The cursor position is projected back onto the nearest peripheral edge ray of `m_TargetFace` using vector dot/cosine math:
  `Vector3 a = m_CurrentPosition - vertices[peripheralEdges[bestIndex].a].position;`
  `Vector3 b = vertices[peripheralEdges[bestIndex].b].position - vertices[peripheralEdges[bestIndex].a].position;`
  `float angle = Vector3.Angle(b, a);`
  `m_CurrentPosition = Vector3.Magnitude(a) * Mathf.Cos(angle * Mathf.Deg2Rad) * b / Vector3.Magnitude(b) + vertices[peripheralEdges[bestIndex].a].position;`

3. Topological Isolation:
- In `DoCut()`, face deletion and polygon regeneration are performed exclusively on `m_TargetFace`: `m_Mesh.DeleteFace(m_TargetFace)`.
- No cross-face spanning paths or continuous multi-face cuts are supported within a single operation. To cut multiple adjacent faces, the user must cut and complete each face sequentially in separate operations.
sections.godot_notes: Godot 4 implementations can extend this architecture if multi-face slicing is desired by utilizing plane slicing or half-edge traversal across shared edges (`WingedEdge.opposite`). In ProBuilder, the constraint to a single face keeps face closure validation deterministic.

sections.heading: STATE MACHINE
sections.content:
The `CutTool` lifecycle, menu integration, and state machine track tool activation, event listening, point placement, dragging, and geometric validation.

1. Tool Registration and Menu Action:
- Tool Attribute: `[EditorTool("Cut Tool", typeof(ProBuilderMesh), typeof(PositionToolContext))]`.
- Menu Action: `UnityEditor.ProBuilder.Actions.CutToolAction` inheriting from `MenuAction`.
  - Toolbar Group: `ToolbarGroup.Tool`.
  - Shortcut: Alt+Shift+C (`keyCommandAlt, keyCommandShift, 'C'`).
  - Valid Modes: `SelectMode.Vertex | SelectMode.Edge | SelectMode.Face`.
  - Enabled Condition: `MeshSelection.selectedObjectCount == 1`.
  - Execution: Toggles tool via `ToolManager.SetActiveTool<CutTool>()` or `ToolManager.RestorePreviousTool()`, then focuses `SceneView.lastActiveSceneView.Focus()`.

2. Lifecycle Callbacks:
- `IsAvailable()`: Returns `true` when `MeshSelection.selectedObjectCount == 1`.
- `OnEnable()`: Initializes `s_HandleColorUseExistingVertex` and `s_HandleColorAddVertexOnEdge` to `Handles.selectedColor`, loads preferences `VertexInsertion.snapToGeometry` (default false) and `VertexInsertion.snappingDistance` (default 0.1f), and loads cursor textures `Cursors/cutCursor` and `Cursors/cutCursor-add`.
- `OnActivated()`: Sets `m_Mesh = MeshSelection.activeMesh`, clears selection `m_Mesh.ClearSelection()`, extracts `m_SelectedVertices` and `m_SelectedEdges`, and subscribes to events: `Undo.undoRedoPerformed += UndoRedoPerformed`, `MeshSelection.objectSelectionChanged += UpdateTarget`, `ProBuilderEditor.selectModeChanged += OnSelectModeChanged`, and `EditorApplication.playModeStateChanged += OnPlayModeStateChanged`.
- `OnWillBeDeactivated()`: Invokes `ExecuteCut(false)` to finalize any pending cut, and unsubscribes from all events.
- `OnPlayModeStateChanged()`: If exiting edit or play mode, calls `ExitTool()`.
- `OnSelectModeChanged()`: Invokes `ToolManager.RestorePreviousPersistentTool()`.
- `UpdateTarget()`: If `MeshSelection.activeMesh != m_Mesh`, calls `Clear()` and rebinds to the newly active mesh.

3. Internal Operational States:
- Idle / Uninitialized (`m_CutPath.Count == 0`, `m_TargetFace == null`): Cursor is `m_CutCursorTexture`. Clicking on empty space passes mouse events to `ProBuilderEditor.instance.HandleMouseEvent`.
- Drawing Path (`m_CutPath.Count > 0`, `m_TargetFace != null`): Cursor is `m_CutAddCursorTexture`. Displays polyline and dotted guide line to the cursor.
- Placing / Dragging Point (`m_PlacingPoint == true` or `m_ModifyingPoint == true` with `m_SelectedIndex >= 0`): Updates existing vertex position on `MouseDrag`.
- Loop Closure State (`isALoop == true`): Detected when `m_CutPath.Count >= 3` and `Math.Approx3(m_CutPath[0].position, m_CutPath[m_CutPath.Count - 1].position)`. Automatically invokes `ExecuteCut()`.
- Cut Validity State (`m_IsCutValid`): Evaluated in `ValidateCutShape()` by performing 2D segment intersection tests using `Math.GetLineSegmentIntersect` on screen-projected coordinates (`HandleUtility.WorldToGUIPoint`). Tests all cut segments against other cut segments and mesh connections. If any segments intersect, `m_IsCutValid = false`, coloring the cut line red and preventing execution.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, custom editor tool state machines can be implemented as `EditorPlugin` sub-modules or `Node3D` gizmo plugins overriding `_forward_3d_gui_input` and `_handles`.

Face and Edge topology structures used for peripheral edge sorting and indexing

Connect edges and vertices operations for mesh subdivision
